one_line: Sultan of Malwa, a hard-driving campaigner and ruler in the Malwa–Gujarat power struggle over trade routes and fortresses.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, lean, battle-hardened build
appearance.face: Oval face with a slightly strong jaw, medium-brown North Indian complexion, sharp dark eyes, straight nose, neatly trimmed pointed beard and moustache, default expression calm but intense with a strategist’s focus
appearance.hair: Thick, dark brown-black hair kept short and tidy beneath a deep green quilted turban-helmet (kulah) wrapped in layered cloth with a subtle gold border, a small rounded steel cap hinted beneath the folds
appearance.costume: Over a long-sleeved, knee-length quilted coat (kazaghand) of muted steel-grey cotton with fine vertical stitching, he wears a sleeveless mail coat that reaches mid-thigh; beneath that, a rich dark green silk jama/gown with side ties and a narrow golden-beige trim at the edges; loose straight trousers in warm cream cotton tucked into mid-calf height leather boots in dark brown; around his waist a broad maroon cloth kamarband sash with a thin patterned gold stripe, with a simple functional leather belt over it holding his scabbard; a short hip-length steel-plated buckler shield slung on his back; minimal jewellery—one plain gold signet ring and small round silver studs at the ears; overall look is practical campaign armour rather than court finery, but fabrics and trims hint at royal status.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged talwar sword with a dark steel blade, disc pommel and an Indo-Persian hilt wrapped in deep red leather, carried at his left hip in a plain dark brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings.

ref_desc: Mahmud Khalji I appears as a lean, medium-brown man with sharp eyes, short hair under a deep green quilted turban-helmet, in steel-grey quilted armour over a dark green jama, cream trousers, maroon sash and dark brown boots, carrying a red-hilted talwar sword.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Mahmud Khalji I of Malwa: a lean, battle-hardened man in his late 30s–40s with an oval medium-brown face, sharp dark eyes, straight nose, and a neatly trimmed pointed beard and moustache, his expression calm but intense like a strategist. His thick dark hair is short and mostly hidden by a deep green quilted turban-helmet wrapped in layered cloth with a subtle gold border, hinting at a small rounded steel cap beneath. He wears a long-sleeved knee-length steel-grey quilted coat with fine vertical stitching, over which sits a sleeveless mail coat reaching mid-thigh, and beneath that a rich dark green silk jama with side ties and a narrow golden-beige trim along the edges. He has loose cream cotton trousers tucked into mid-calf dark brown leather boots. Around his waist is a broad maroon cloth kamarband sash with a thin patterned gold stripe, cinched by a plain functional leather belt that supports a dark brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings. A small steel-plated buckler shield rests on his back, and he has only a plain gold signet ring and tiny round silver ear studs for jewellery. His signature weapon is a slightly curved single-edged talwar with a dark steel blade, disc pommel, and an Indo-Persian hilt wrapped in deep red leather, worn at his left hip. Use a palette dominated by dark green, steel grey, cream, maroon, dark brown, and touches of gold, and present front, back, and a close-up of the head to clearly show face, hair, armour layers, sash, boots, and talwar design.
